system.name: DarwinGame
system.one_liner: a tournament-based performance tuner that compares application configurations reliably under interference-prone, noisy cloud environments

content.subject: how DarwinGame's tournament narrows a large pool of candidate configurations down to one winner through four differently-styled phases

panels.label: Regional Phase (Swiss Style)
panels.differs: the full grid of candidate configurations is grouped by region and played Swiss-style; the most promising (dark green) configurations progress out of the full white-dot grid

panels.label: Global Phase (Double Elimination Style)
panels.differs: regional winners compete in a circular double-elimination bracket with a Main Bracket and Loser Bracket, scored by Consistency and Execution Score

panels.label: Playoffs (Barrage Style)
panels.differs: a small surviving set plays a cyclic barrage-style round to further narrow the field

panels.label: Final
panels.differs: the two remaining configurations are compared to pick the single tuning-configuration winner

content.key_idea: DarwinGame structures configuration selection as a four-phase tournament, from Swiss-style regional play through double-elimination and barrage-style playoffs to a final, so that noisy single comparisons don't eliminate a good configuration too early.
content.reading_order: left to right through the four phases: the Regional Phase grid, the Global Phase's circular double-elimination brackets (Main/Loser), the Playoffs barrage cluster, and the Final pair, with white vs dark-green dots marking surviving vs winning configurations throughout

summary: This figure gives an overview of DarwinGame's tournament-based tuning procedure, which narrows a large pool of candidate application configurations down to one winner across four phases with different playing styles. The Regional Phase (Swiss Style) first splits the whole search space into regions and plays each Swiss-style, promoting the most promising configurations (dark green dots) out of the full grid (white dots). Winners advance into the Global Phase (Double Elimination Style), where a Main Bracket and Loser Bracket, scored by Consistency Score and Execution Score, give losing configurations a second chance rather than eliminating them outright. Survivors proceed to Playoffs (Barrage Style), a small cyclic round among the remaining top candidates, before the tournament converges on a single Final comparison that picks the winning tuning configuration. Consistent white/dark-green dot colouring across all four differently-shaped phases lets the reader track survival versus elimination even as the visual metaphor for each phase changes.
summary_zh: 该图展示DarwinGame基于锦标赛的调优流程：区域赛（瑞士轮）从整片配置网格中选出优胜者（深绿点）；全局赛（双败淘汰制）用一致性分和执行分在主/败者组中评选；季后赛（barrage赛制）进一步淘汰；最终决赛选出唯一获胜配置。
notes: content.base corrected from the prior 'none' (not a valid v3 base value) to 'mixed', since the four phases are drawn with different visual metaphors (grid, circular bracket, small cyclic cluster, pair). style.palette reflects only the one vector fill (#f78d1e) found in the source-SVG histogram; roughly 82% of the figure's area is embedded raster images (per the measured attributes), which is where the grid/bracket colours and the green/white configuration dots actually live, so their hex values do not appear in the histogram.
